The Wednesday Note

The backup plan still counts.

For the day your original plan has absolutely no chance.

There is a version of a healthy routine that looks great on paper. You have time for the full workout. Dinner is planned. Everyone cooperates.

And then there is Wednesday.

The meeting runs over. One kid needs something. You realize at 4:30 that the chicken is still frozen. Suddenly, the plan you made on Sunday feels like it belongs to a completely different person.

Most people treat that moment like a test: do the whole plan, or admit the day is a loss.

But the smaller version is not the fake version.

Ten minutes of movement is not pretending to work out. A rotisserie chicken and microwave rice are not a nutrition failure. Going to bed instead of forcing a late workout can be the choice that helps tomorrow happen.

The goal is not to win every Wednesday. The goal is to have a plan that still knows what to do when Wednesday wins.

Your backup plan needs a name.

“I’ll do less if I get busy” is easy to negotiate away. Make it specific enough that tired-you does not have to invent it.

Try this today

Write one if/then sentence.

If my planned workout does not happen, then I will walk for ten minutes after dinner. If dinner falls apart, then I will build a plate from one protein, one easy carb, and whatever fruit or vegetable is available.

Pick one. Keep it almost embarrassingly doable. Then let it count.

Kelsey
